title: London session of the USD bond market recommended closed all day for Easter Monday — the cause of the Tokyo half-close already tracked on this date
source: NEWS: sifma.org/resources/guides-playbooks/holiday-schedule ('Holiday Schedule'), fetched direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 298,926 bytes) and parsed twice by this session — card-by-card off the rendered DOM with region attribution fixed to the page's own 'U.S. / U.K. / Japan Holiday Recommendations' <h2> headings at byte offsets 36,537 / 47,499 / 60,383, then independently out of the page's embedded Next.js flight payload (127 cards across all six panels), which is where the 2027 tabs live behind a control the DOM parse never sees. The U.K. 2027 panel reads exactly ['Easter Monday', 'Monday, March 29, 2027'] with NO early-close note attached — the full-closure shape, and consistent with every other U.K. card: the panel carries 36 cards across 2026 and 2027 and ZERO 'Early Close' strings in either year, where the U.S. 2026 panel carries eight and the Japan 2026 panel two. The causing holiday is independently statutory: gov.uk/bank-holidays.json (HTTP 200, 22,207 bytes, the England-and-Wales division) lists '2027-03-29 | Easter Monday'. New York trades a full session that day — Good Friday falls 2027-03-26 and is already tracked as good-friday-market-closure-2027-03-26, and the SIFMA U.S. 2027 panel's Good Friday card carries a 'Early Close (2:00 p.m. Eastern Time): Thursday, March 25, 2027' note with no 03-29 entry of any kind. Filed estimate on three counts, identical to the six sifma-* entries already on this calendar: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for an industry trade association's recommended schedule, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and SIFMA's own page states its schedule is a recommendation rather than a market-wide halt each firm is bound by.
notes: DISCOVERED during the sifma-uk-bond-market-closure-2026-12-28 initial research (2026-09-05), leg 16. WHY IT EARNS A ROW: this calendar already tracks TWO CONSEQUENCES of this holiday on this exact date without their cause — sifma-japan-early-close-2027-03-29 (Tokyo's USD desk half-closing at 15:00 JST, a card SIFMA files under the British holiday that causes it) and boj-summary-of-opinions-2027-03-29. It is the exact configuration of sifma-uk-bond-market-closure-2026-12-28 recurring: London recommended fully closed, Tokyo recommended closed early, New York running a normal session. SCOPE, verbatim from SIFMA's page: 'All SIFMA holiday recommendations apply to the trading of U.S. dollar-denominated government securities, mortgage- and asset-backed securities, over-the-counter investment-grade and high-yield corporate bonds, municipal bonds and secondary money market trading in bankers' acceptances, commercial paper and Yankee and Euro certificates of deposit' — so the three regional panels are three TIME ZONES of one US-dollar market, not three asset classes. GILTS ARE OUT OF SCOPE; this is London's dollar desk, and the title says so deliberately. IMPACT LOW, and the 12-28 lane measured why: this card is REDUNDANT WITH STATUTE. Easter Monday is a gov.uk bank holiday, so London is dark regardless of what SIFMA recommends — ^FTSE printed no bar on 37 of 37 gov.uk weekday bank holidays that were New York sessions since 2019 (detector = a weekday with a ^GSPC bar and no ^FTSE bar, 37/38 precision, the one false positive being the 2020-12-22 Yahoo data gap). That is the opposite of the US-panel closures sifma-bond-market-closure-2026-11-11 and -2026-10-12, where NYSE trades a full session and the SIFMA card IS the information. MEASURED, not assumed, and it is a triple null: across 170 London-shut/New-York-open sessions since 1990, ^GSPC's mean |close-to-close| runs 0.702% against 0.745% month-matched (Welch t = -0.64); EWU's volume gap to SPY does not clear a month-and-weekday-matched control (permutation p = 0.096, n = 140 vs 971); EWU's volatility compression is not attributable to its dark underlying (paired against EWJ, whose Tokyo underlying is open, -0.086 with 74/142 negative, p = 0.337, while FXB — whose FX market never closes at all — compresses most); and EWU adds nothing over SPY about where the FTSE reopens (b = 0.064, t = 0.48, R-squared 0.131 -> 0.133). No house playbook is calendar-, holiday- or rates-keyed (docs/plans/trade-playbooks.md and docs/research/multi-symbol-sweep.md grepped 2026-09-05 for 'holiday|gilt|london|boxing|sifma|closure|ewu|ftse|year-end': zero hits in both), and this repo tracks no UK-listed symbol. HONEST LIMIT: the U.K. 2027 panel is internally inconsistent at year-end — it reads 'Christmas Day / Friday, December 24, 2027' and 'Boxing Day / None' while gov.uk dates statutory substitutes on 2027-12-27 and 2027-12-28, and it lists Juneteenth on a Saturday and July 4 on a Sunday unshifted where the U.S. panel shifts both — so it reads as a loosely-maintained mirror of US statutory dates. Against that, NO U.K. card in either year carries a tentative flag, where every 2027 Japan card reads 'Tentative - Subject to confirmation by the Bank of Japan'. This entry is filed on the published 2027 U.K. card alone and should be re-verified against a re-fetch before the date. It is a recommendation to member firms, NOT an exchange closure; the London Stock Exchange's own calendar is a client-rendered page carrying no machine-readable holiday data (fetched 2026-09-05, HTTP 200, 54,995 bytes, body strips to five text cells), so the equity-hours claim here is empirical rather than sourced from the exchange.
